feedback: based on my feedback for the cdi-support.md file, is there anything you'd like to update in docker-specialized before I suggest edits?
category: application of prior feedback to another section
agent_rationale: Lead with reader configuration and GPU visibility; describe profile-path and container-start outcomes; omit atomic-write implementation detail from procedural prose while retaining the detail in release notes; retain short noun references and one sentence per source line.

changes.before:
Legacy mode limits EGL and Vulkan visibility to the physical GPUs assigned to a container when the `graphics` or `display` driver capability is enabled.
In CDI and JIT-CDI modes, the `update-application-profile` hook applies the same limits.

The `update-application-profile` hook replaces the application profile atomically.
If the profile path is a symbolic link, the hook replaces the symbolic link and leaves the link target unchanged.
Read-only filesystem errors and busy-file errors do not prevent the container from starting, but the application-profile hook cannot update the profile when either error occurs.

If the application-profile hook conflicts with an application, refer to
[Disabling Hooks in JIT-CDI Mode](cdi-support.md#disabling-hooks-in-jit-cdi-mode).
changes.after:
When you enable the `graphics` or `display` driver capability in legacy mode, EGL and Vulkan applications can see only the physical GPUs assigned to the container.
In CDI and JIT-CDI modes, the `update-application-profile` hook applies the same visibility limits.

If you use a symbolic link for the application profile path, the hook replaces the symbolic link and leaves the link target unchanged.
Your container can start even if a read-only filesystem or busy-file error prevents the hook from updating the application profile.

If the hook conflicts with your application, refer to [Disabling Hooks in JIT-CDI Mode](cdi-support.md#disabling-hooks-in-jit-cdi-mode).

feedback: more feedback that I am certain I have supplied many times in the past.  Avoid anthropomorphisms like "see".  Do not ascribe human qualities to inanimate objects.
reusable_preference: Do not ascribe human qualities or actions to software, applications, or other inanimate objects. Replace anthropomorphic wording such as "applications can see" with a precise description of the technical behavior or outcome.

changes.after: When you enable the `graphics` or `display` driver capability in legacy mode, GPU visibility for EGL and Vulkan applications is limited to the physical GPUs assigned to the container.

category: release notes describing the problem and affected configuration
reusable_preference: Lead bug-fix release notes with the problem affecting readers and the configuration in which it occurs, rather than the implementation change. Verify the problem from source material; do not invent a reported failure.
evidence_note: Original PR #2146 describes prevention of runtime device injection through volume mounts with accept-nvidia-visible-devices-as-volume-mounts=true. PR body and fetched discussion do not link a user-reported failure. Default false was verified in api/config/v1/config.go previously.

changes.before:
- Generated CDI specifications now prevent duplicate device injection when the NVIDIA Container Runtime accepts device requests through volume mounts.
  The specification adds a `void` volume mount that suppresses volume-mount device requests, so the runtime does not inject devices in addition to the CDI-selected devices.
  For more information, refer to [PR #2184](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2184).
changes.after:
- Fixed an issue where volume-mount requests could add GPUs to a container in addition to the GPUs selected through CDI.
  This issue affected configurations with `accept-nvidia-visible-devices-as-volume-mounts` set to `true`.
  The setting defaults to `false`.
  For more information, refer to [PR #2184](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2184).

feedback: "built-in applet" seems like a distraction from the change that now the host binaries are run.
reusable_preference: State the changed behavior directly. Omit implementation terms that distract from the outcome, such as BusyBox built-in applets when the relevant change is execution of host binaries.

changes.before:
- The toolkit container now uses a BusyBox build that runs host binaries when executing commands through `chroot`.
  Previously, BusyBox could run a built-in applet instead of the requested host binary.
  For more information, refer to [PR #2189](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2189) and [issue #299 in /NVIDIA/k8s-driver-manager](https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-driver-manager/issues/299).
changes.after:
- Commands run through `chroot` in the toolkit container now execute the host binaries.
  For more information, refer to [PR #2189](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2189) and [issue #299 in /NVIDIA/k8s-driver-manager](https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-driver-manager/issues/299).

feedback: better, but still feels vague and unnecessary without the detail of "...host binaries, such as modprobe, to ensure kernel modules are loaded correctly."
reusable_preference: When removing implementation detail, retain a concrete example and the practical consequence needed to explain why the change matters. Concision must not leave a release note vague or apparently unnecessary.

changes.before: - Commands run through `chroot` in the toolkit container now execute the host binaries.
changes.after: - Commands run through `chroot` in the toolkit container now execute host binaries, such as `modprobe`, so kernel modules and their dependencies load correctly.
